styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Night markets, beef noodles and dumplings all day.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Temples, museums and old streets in the city core.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Hot springs, hills and easy day trips out of town.

stays.why: Young, busy and central. Walk to the MRT, night markets and the old Wanhua temples. Good for first-timers who want nightlife.
Quiet lanes, small shops and cafés. Two MRT lines and short rides to most sights.
Leafy and calm, near the park and Yongkang Street food. A good base for couples and slower trips.
Best for transport: MRT, trains and the airport line in one place. Practical for short stays and day trips.

food: Eat at night markets: Shilin and Raohe are the big ones. Go hungry, share dishes, and carry small cash.
Try the classics: beef noodle soup, soup dumplings, oyster omelette, stinky tofu and shaved ice.
Yongkang Street in Da'an is good for a sit-down food walk with tea shops and dessert.
Convenience stores are cheap and open late. A quick meal or snack costs about NT$60–150.
Many small eateries are cash-first. Keep some TWD on you; card use is common but not everywhere.
more_time: Add a day trip to Jiufen and the coast by bus or train; check times on the day.
Take a hot-spring trip to Beitou on the MRT, about 30 minutes from the center.
Swap one city day for the National Palace Museum if you like art and history; allow half a day.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the night markets, temples and museums, plus one day trip to the hills or hot springs.

month_notes: Jan: cool and damp, highs near 19°C. Pack a jacket and an umbrella.
Feb: similar to Jan, around 20°C. Rain on about 11 days.
Mar: warming to 23°C. A good shoulder month with fewer crowds.
Apr: mild and pleasant at 26°C, but rain days rise to 14.
May: warm and wet. Expect showers on about 19 days.
Jun: hot and rainy, highs near 31°C. Plan indoor breaks.
Jul: hottest month, around 33°C, with 18 rain days. Go out early and late.
Aug: still very hot at 32°C and wet. Carry water.
Sep: hot at 30°C but rain eases a little.
Oct: comfortable at 27°C. A strong month to visit.
Nov: mild at 25°C with 13 rain days. Good for walking.
Dec: cooler at 20°C and damp. Bring layers.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical and humid. Summers are hot and wet; winters are mild but grey and damp. Rain falls in every month.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect 11–21 rain days each month. June is the wettest. Always carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Hot, humid summer
items.text: July and August reach about 33°C with high humidity. Plan indoor sights at midday.

items.title: Best months: October to April
items.text: Highs of 19–27°C and less intense heat. Best for walking and day trips.

items.title: Mild winter
items.text: January and February sit around 14–20°C. A light jacket is enough; indoor spaces can feel cold.

items.title: Typhoon season
items.text: Late summer and early autumn can bring storms. Check forecasts on the day and keep plans flexible.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers, a rain jacket or umbrella, and comfortable shoes. Add a warm layer for winter evenings.

transit.best: MRT for most trips; EasyCard makes it cheaper and works on buses too.

modes.text: Clean, safe and cheap: NT$20–65 per ride. Trains run about 06:00–00:00. EasyCard gives 20% off.
Frequent city buses. Pay with EasyCard on boarding; transfers within an hour cost NT$7.
Metered taxis are plentiful and Uber operates in Taipei. Good for late nights and luggage.
Not advised for visitors. Parking is hard and scooters dominate the roads.
Sidewalks are good in central areas. YouBike share bikes are widely available for longer hops.
